summary: Georg Ludolf Dissen was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1804–1807). He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1818–1824) and the University of Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy (~1826–1829), later serving as a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen in 1829.

Georg Morgenstierne specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oslo, Bonn, Berlin, and under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at the University of Gothenburg (1930–1937) and Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1876–1881). He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1885 to 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, under Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, and at Jena. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1801–1805), Heidelberg University (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and Göttingen (PhD, 1965) and served at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977; attested 2026) and as professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. Educated at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden, he held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889).

George A. Kennedy worked in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke (~1932–1937) and held a post at Yale University from around 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA (PhD 2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and others. He held posts at CU Boulder (2001) and the University of Saskatchewan (attested 2019).

George Abraham Grierson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1873), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1873–1898), as Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and as Governor at SOAS (1917–1925).
George C. O. Haas was an Indologist. He served as recording secretary for the American Oriental Society (attested 1915) and as an editor of the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

George Cardona is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned degrees from NYU and Yale, studying under Paul Thieme and Warren Crawford Cowgill, alongside traditional teachers. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1965 to 2006.

George Chemparathy is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and as a professor at Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963), and held posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2008).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1863), where he later held an academic post from around 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès specialized in archaeology, Indology, and sinology, studying at EPHE under Finot, Lévi, and Foucher. He headed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929) and directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1929–1947), later serving as curator at Musée d'Ennery (1947–1969).

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD from Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he became Professor of Religion around 1974.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George Derwent Thomson was a scholar in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at King's College, Cambridge, and Trinity College Dublin, and held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (~1927–1931) and the University of Birmingham (~1937–1970).

George Devereux studied in Paris—including under Marcel Mauss—and at UC Berkeley. He later held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1963–1985) and Paris Descartes University (~1970–1978).
